questions.question: A favorite glass vase shatters in the living room while your parents are out. What is your immediate reaction?

options.A: Inspect the pieces and interrogate your siblings to figure out exactly whose fault it was.
options.B: Mentally calculate the probability of your mom finding out before you can buy a replacement.
options.C: Come up with a 'sibling treaty' where everyone chips in Rs. 50 a month for a 'Broken Items Fund'.
options.D: Take charge, order everyone to clean it up, and decide the official excuse so nobody gets in trouble.

questions.question: It's super cloudy, and you have to walk/cycle to school. How do you handle the rain threat?

options.A: Look at the puddles and the soil outside to check if it has already rained nearby.
options.B: Check three different weather apps to find the exact percentage chance of rain per hour.
options.C: Invent a cool jugaad by turning a large plastic bag into a waterproof cover for your heavy school bag.
options.D: Tell your friends to carry umbrellas and keep a spare Rs. 50 for an auto-rickshaw just in case.

questions.question: Your gully cricket tournament is tomorrow, but the pitch (the street) is totally uneven and full of potholes.

options.A: Go to the pitch, inspect the cracks closely, and check if the rival team tampered with it.
options.B: Calculate how the uneven bounce will negatively affect your team's overall run rate.
options.C: Create a new set of 'gully rules' specifically for this pitch (e.g., one-tip-one-hand is allowed).
options.D: Manage the team's strategy, decide who bowls from which end, and negotiate with the umpire.

questions.question: Your older sibling gets a traffic challan from the police for not wearing a helmet. What do you do?

options.A: Demand to see the traffic camera CCTV footage to prove they were actually wearing it at the signal.
options.B: Calculate how much pocket money they've lost this year purely on challans versus the cost of a good helmet.
options.C: Sketch an idea for a smart scooty that simply won't start unless the helmet is strapped on.
options.D: Enforce a strict house rule: no helmet, no scooty keys. End of discussion.

questions.question: Your best friend drops their phone and the screen completely shatters.

options.A: Question them on exactly *how* and *where* it fell to see if the warranty will still cover it.
options.B: Analyze the exact cost of repair at a local shop in the market versus the official service center.
options.C: Suggest starting a 'phone emergency pool' where your friend group saves 10 rupees a week for screen fixes.
options.D: Take their phone, confidently bargain with the local repair guy, and get it fixed smoothly for them.

questions.question: The class is going on a school trip to a water park. What is your role in the group?

options.A: Go check the rides first to make sure they are safe and working properly before anyone gets on.
options.B: Figure out the exact per-person budget for extra food, locker tickets, and travel snacks.
options.C: Create a fun 'fast-track' game where whoever wins gets to skip the line for the best water slide.
options.D: Become the group captain, keep everyone together, and handle any arguments with the teachers.

questions.question: You completely forgot to do your math homework, and the teacher is checking notebooks.

options.A: Hunt for proof on the class WhatsApp group that the teacher never actually announced the deadline.
options.B: Count how many times she has checked your row this month to guess the probability of getting caught.
options.C: Invent an elaborate, highly convincing story about a power cut, a street dog, and a missing notebook.
options.D: Apologize upfront, promise to submit it tomorrow during recess, and negotiate your way out of punishment.

questions.question: The school canteen ran out of samosas right before your turn in line.

options.A: Question the seniors in front to see if someone unfairly bought 10 samosas for themselves.
options.B: Calculate the exact time you need to leave class tomorrow to beat the canteen rush.
options.C: Suggest the canteen uncle start a 'pre-booking token system' so nobody misses out.
options.D: Organize your friends to quickly buy different available items and share a massive mixed lunch instead.

questions.question: It's Diwali night, and your younger cousins are bursting firecrackers.

options.A: Stand near the rockets to make sure nobody has placed the bottles dangerously close to the neighbor's car.
options.B: Track how many crackers misfire and figure out the 'dud rate' of the brand you bought.
options.C: Come up with a fun new light-painting photography idea using only the safe sparklers (phuljharis).
options.D: Supervise the entire event, keep the sand and water buckets ready, and manage the chaos safely.

questions.question: Final exams are next week, and the whole friend group is stressing out.

options.A: Hunt down the previous five years' question papers to investigate patterns in what actually gets asked.
options.B: Divide the syllabus by pages and calculate exactly how many minutes you need per chapter to finish.
options.C: Make colorful mind-maps and funny Hindi acronyms to help everyone remember boring history dates.
options.D: Set a strict group-study schedule for your friends and ensure nobody gets distracted by their phones.

Claim_Investigator.title: The Truth Seeker (Claim Investigator / Surveyor)
Claim_Investigator.primary_match_text: You have a sharp eye for detail and love getting to the bottom of a mystery. You don't just accept things at face value; you look for the evidence!
Claim_Investigator.day_in_the_life: Traveling to the sites of car accidents, factory fires, or burglaries. Interviewing people, taking photographs, and acting like a detective to find out if an insurance claim is genuine or a fraud.
Claim_Investigator.alternative_match_text: If not this, you'd make a great Forensic Expert, Journalist, or Private Detective.
Claim_Investigator.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Any Stream (Commerce/Science preferred). College: B.Com, B.Sc, or BBA. Professional: Complete a Diploma/Certification in Insurance Surveying and loss assessment from IIISLA (Indian Institute of Insurance Surveyors and Loss Assessors).

Actuary.title: The Math Magician (Actuary / Risk Analyst)
Actuary.primary_match_text: You see the world in numbers, logic, and patterns. You love calculating odds and using data to predict what might happen next.
Actuary.day_in_the_life: Sitting in a high-tech office, using advanced math and statistics to calculate the probability of risks (like earthquakes or illnesses). You decide exactly how much an insurance premium should cost so the company stays profitable.
Actuary.alternative_match_text: If not this, you'd make a great Data Scientist, Statistician, or Investment Banker.
Actuary.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce with Maths or PCM (Science). College: B.Sc Statistics, B.Sc Mathematics, or B.Com. Professional: Clear the ACET (Actuarial Common Entrance Test) and pass the rigorous professional exams conducted by the Institute of Actuaries of India (IAI).

Policy_Designer.title: The Idea Generator (Custom Policy Product Designer)
Policy_Designer.primary_match_text: You are highly creative and love designing out-of-the-box solutions. You realize that boring problems need fresh, exciting answers.
Policy_Designer.day_in_the_life: Brainstorming and inventing entirely new insurance products. You might design 'pet health insurance', 'wedding cancellation insurance', or even 'concert rain insurance'. You make the rules for what is covered and what isn't.
Policy_Designer.alternative_match_text: If not this, you'd make a great Product Manager, Marketing Strategist, or Entrepreneur.
Policy_Designer.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce or Arts. College: BBA, B.Com, or BA Economics. Professional: Pursue an MBA in Insurance & Risk Management, Marketing, or a PG Diploma from the National Insurance Academy (NIA), Pune.

Risk_Director.title: The Mastermind (Risk Management Director)
Risk_Director.primary_match_text: You are a natural leader who keeps everyone safe while looking at the big picture. You know how to manage money, handle people, and prepare for the worst.
Risk_Director.day_in_the_life: Sitting in the boardroom, overseeing the entire company's money. You make the big decisions on which risks are worth taking, ensuring the business survives market crashes, natural disasters, or pandemics.
Risk_Director.alternative_match_text: If not this, you'd make a great CEO, Chief Financial Officer (CFO), or Business Head.
Risk_Director.educational_roadmap: 11th/12th: Commerce (with or without Maths). College: BBA, B.Com, or B.A. Economics. Professional: MBA in Finance or Risk Management from a top tier IIM/B-School, and global certifications like FRM (Financial Risk Manager).
